set.t: Kent County park (Wabasis Lake Park, former Tower farm, county-owned since c.1930): look-only, no digging without county permission. The other candidate, the creek above the lake from the Stocking family account, is the pin 'Chief John Wabasis' kettle of treaty money'. 1894 plate: 'C. O. Tower 35' in the E part of NE¼ sec 29 on the N-S road to the NW shore of the W lobe (M. A. Tower 40 W of it; S. Tower 40 in S sec 29). Lidar: an oval pitted enclosure at 43.1419,-85.3979 on the Tower land, 300 m NW of the cut bank, is unexplained (old gravel digging or root cellars?); worth a look.
acc: Kent County park: look-only, no digging without county permission
pinev: 1894 plat: C. O. Tower in NE¼ sec 29 T9N R9W where a road meets the NW shore; state lidar shows a ~300 m cut bank between the old road and the shore, centred about 43.140,-85.395; r200 covers the bank
Kent County parks layer (ArcGIS): the pin is inside Wabasis County Park, about 70 m from its north edge; the r200 ring runs slightly past the boundary onto private land.

tw-mi-wabasis-tower-road-bank-caves.st: In Aug 1929 Clyde O. Tower offered his 35 acres on Wabasis Lake (in the family since 1838) to the Kent road commission for $1,500; by 1931 it was a 35-acre county park circling a bay, improved in 1930.

tw-mi-wabasis-lake-gold.st: The Belding Banner (4 Oct 1916) says Barney Race and Ed Whitford probed the shore of Little Wabasis Lake for the kettle; the 1922 Stocking letter names the Olsgaard farm north of Belding as the family place.
